human_summary.problem: RedCap had already moved long-lived assets under assets/, but the root still looked noisy because host entries, runtime source, compatibility symlinks, local state and Prism evidence were all visible together.
human_summary.solution: Treat the root as a small set of deliberate product, host, runtime, asset, evidence and local-state zones. Keep compatibility anchors only where they protect old scripts, reports and receipts; make new writes use canonical assets/ paths.
human_summary.effect: Humans and Agents can now distinguish 'kept because it is a product/runtime entry' from 'kept only as a compatibility bridge' and from 'local state that must never be packaged'.

claim_boundary.allowed_user_claim: RASG-029 closes the non-release engineering-directory confusion by giving every visible root class an owner, lifecycle, package disposition and human explanation. It does not delete receipt anchors, erase Prism raw evidence or authorize a public release.
forbidden_claims: All old compatibility path names disappeared.
All prism/runs evidence was physically cleared.
Package exclusion alone proves historical assets were cleaned.

canonical_asset_roots.role: Specs, research, traces, catalog and recent task reports.
canonical_asset_roots.write_rule: New docs and reports write here first; compatibility entry is read-only bridge.

canonical_asset_roots.role: Active lessons, runtime memory explanations, host knowledge and LLM-wiki-lite.
canonical_asset_roots.write_rule: New knowledge writes here first and must remain index-first.

canonical_asset_roots.role: Machine contracts, policies, ledgers, package rules, backlog and lookup dictionary.
canonical_asset_roots.write_rule: This is the real control-plane asset location; root references is a compatibility symlink.

canonical_asset_roots.role: Formal Prism reports only, not raw runs.
canonical_asset_roots.write_rule: Formal reports may be archived here; raw run evidence remains under prism/runs lifecycle.

canonical_asset_roots.role: Private cold archive for old reports, old research and trace evidence.
canonical_asset_roots.write_rule: Private archive is not public-package content and must be exact-read only.

root_zone_model.why_visible_at_root: They are the first human reading surface and should stay short, explanatory and package-visible.
Host tools discover fixed filenames or folders. These entries must stay thin and point back to RedCap's single source of truth.
They are install/run entry points. Moving them before the release profile is finalized would break the package/runtime contract.
Package managers and git expect these surfaces at the root.
This is the consolidated parent for docs, knowledge, references, formal evidence and private archive.
They are symlinks or compatibility bridges kept so old reports, receipts and scripts remain resolvable.
These are source and contract layers, not historical asset piles. A future public runtime profile may split them, but not as an unsafe cleanup side effect.
Prism is both executable review tooling and raw evidence lifecycle. Reports are bridged to assets/evidence; raw runs remain local evidence.
Layer A remains a product boundary decision; moving or deleting it would be a release/product-scope action.
These are ignored/private/local state and must never be public package or shared knowledge.
Templates are public starter material, not live shared knowledge. External redcap-arsenal remains the real shared knowledge worktree.

compatibility_anchor_policy.default_position: Retain compatibility anchors when they protect old receipts, old reports, host discovery or script consumers.
compatibility_anchor_policy.not_a_completion_gap: A legacy-looking path name is not automatically a failure if it is a symlink/bridge with a canonical assets/ target and package exclusion is proven where needed.
compatibility_anchor_policy.future_removal_rule: Any physical removal must have a separate task card, alias map, rollback plan, consumer matrix, package proof, Prism review and closeout receipt.

current_inventory.retention_days_note: This is the stale-age threshold used by the lifecycle tool when classifying safe local residues. It is not an automatic deletion timer; apply still requires an explicit lifecycle command and cited evidence remains protected.

policy: Do not delete cited formal evidence or named local evidence.
Only prune acceptance fixture residue through the lifecycle tool and only when the tool reports purgeable items.
A full raw-evidence archive or deletion policy remains a release-risk decision, not a normal cleanup shortcut.

package_surface_result.release_boundary: Public package eligibility is still controlled by package safety and release-readiness tasks; this manifest does not authorize publication.

formal_release_task_must_recheck: whether any compatibility anchor should be hidden, copied or removed for the public package profile
whether Prism raw run evidence should be archived, compressed or pruned beyond the safe acceptance set
whether Layer A loom remains public scope, internal scope or retired scope
whether control-plane source should be split into maintainer-only and runtime-public profiles
